story: Section 69(3) of the Consumer Protection Act says I must wait 90 days after the seller refuses before I can complain, correct? I ordered a gas stove for Rs 11,200 online, it arrived broken on 4 October 2026 and they refused a refund by email on 6 October 2026. I live in Guwahati.

timeline.user_words: they refused a refund by email on 6 October 2026

facts.user_goal: Complain about a broken gas stove and get a refund

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 06 Oct 2028 (698 days left). This counts 2 years from 06 Oct 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 11,200, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

support.text: You are a consumer because you bought goods for personal use for Rs 11,200.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as a person who buys goods for consideration, which includes 'any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised'. The sentence applies this to the person's facts (Rs 11,200 paid for personal use goods). The amount and personal use are the person's own facts, not added legal conditions.

support.text: The broken gas stove is a defect in the goods.
support.reason: 'Defect' is defined as 'any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard... in relation to any goods or product'. A broken gas stove is a fault/imperfection in the goods, which directly falls within this definition.

support.text: Refusing a refund for a broken item is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods... and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days' is an unfair trade practice. The sentence applies this to the person's facts (broken item).

support.text: Your complaint goes to the District Commission because you paid Rs 11,200.
support.reason: The law text states District Commission consideration is 'up to Rs 50 lakh'. The sentence applies this to the person's facts (Rs 11,200 paid, which is within the up to Rs 50 lakh limit). The amount is the person's own fact.

support.text: There is no filing fee because you paid Rs 11,200.
support.reason: The law text states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' The sentence applies this to the person's facts (Rs 11,200 paid, which is within the up to Rs 5 lakh limit). The amount is the person's own fact.

support.text: You can file your complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
support.reason: The law text states 'Provided that the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed.' This supports electronic filing. The sentence applies this to the person's facts (specifying e-jagriti.gov.in, which is an electronic filing method).

support.text: You must file your complaint within 2 years from 6 October 2026.
support.reason: The law text states the complaint must be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen, not from a fixed future date like 6 October 2026. The sentence adds a specific future date that is not in the law text.

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
